title: Be the world leader
note: Illustrative. Each policy removes a share of the current path's CO₂ emissions, ramping in over six years. Warming follows cumulative CO₂. Real policies overlap and behave less neatly. This is a game, not a forecast.

policies.title: Carbon price
policies.blurb: Charge polluters for every tonne of CO₂.

policies.title: Phase out coal power
policies.blurb: Close coal plants on a fixed schedule.

policies.title: Wind and solar build-out
policies.blurb: Faster permits and grid links for wind and solar.

policies.title: End fossil fuel subsidies
policies.blurb: Stop paying to keep oil, gas and coal cheap.

policies.title: Low-carbon firm power and grids
policies.blurb: Reliable clean power and a stronger grid.

policies.title: Efficient buildings
policies.blurb: Insulation and heat pumps for homes and offices.

policies.title: Clean steel and cement
policies.blurb: Help factories switch to low-carbon methods.

policies.title: Public transport
policies.blurb: More trains, buses and safe cycling routes.

policies.title: Less food waste
policies.blurb: Rules and campaigns that cut waste and meat-heavy meals.

verdicts.title: Steward of the century
verdicts.line: You bent the curve about as far as these rules allow.

verdicts.title: Bold reformer
verdicts.line: Strong early action. Most of the gain came from moving first.

verdicts.title: Reluctant reformer
verdicts.line: Real cuts, but too few or too late to change the century much.

verdicts.title: Slow mover
verdicts.line: Some progress. The current path was already doing most of the work.

verdicts.title: Bystander
verdicts.line: Little changed. The world stays on its current path.
